newsitem.title: UK: UK's Axa Equity & Law says float pure speculation.
newsitem.headline: UK's Axa Equity & Law says float pure speculation.

text.p: Axa Equity & Law, the UK subsidiary of French insurer Axa on Friday denied a newspaper report that it was considering a partial stock market flotation.
"It's pure speculation, it has no foundation. What we think is that this is based on analysts' speculation. It has certainly not come out of Axa Equity & Law," spokesman Peter Webb told Reuters.
Speculation had probably been fuelled by news earlier this week that Axa was merging with another French insurer, UAP, Webb added.
London's Independent newspaper said Axa Equity and Law was considering a partial flotation that could raise up to 400 million stg ($665 million).
Axa Equity & Law, whose principal business is life insurance, pensions and investments, had total new business in 1995 of 842 million stg, up from 813 million the year before.
Group assets at the end of 1995 were 11.2 billion stg and the workforce numbered aroubd 1,900. Pre-tax profits were 50.8 million stg.
-- Reuters Insurance News 44 171 542 2769 ($ = 0.601 British Pounds Sterling)
